problem: Cross-modal grounding between language instructions and visual observations in VLN is weak in prior visual encoders, which limits how well the agent aligns instruction phrases with what it sees.
motivation: Successful VLN depends on robust grounding of instructions in visual inputs. The authors observe that attention mechanisms strengthen semantic alignment between vision and language, and they compare convolutional and transformer-based visual encoders to test this.
key_idea: Replace or augment the VLN visual encoder with an attention-based (transformer-style) encoder to improve vision-language semantic alignment.
insight: Only the abstract is available. It claims that attention-based encoders align visual and linguistic modalities better than convolutional ones, based on an empirical comparison of CNN and transformer architectures. No ablation details can be cited.
method: Attention-based visual encoder: replaces or augments the visual feature extractor with attention/transformer-based architectures to strengthen cross-modal grounding (details not available from the abstract)
Empirical comparison: convolutional versus transformer-based visual encoders evaluated on R2R
